lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Hedged the bank's interest-rate risk on its fixed-rate bond holdings by buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
- Cut the monthly close from 8 working days to 5 by automating 30 reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Mapping 600 general-ledger accounts to a new chart of accounts, rebuilding the allocation rules and testing them against two prior closes, cut manual journal entries from 350 to 90 a month.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Trained 5 plant controllers on the new budgeting template and wrote its user guide.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Showed the share value fell from USD 50 to USD 40, a 25% drop, when the discount rate rose by 1 point.
- Raised the model's forecast accuracy by 12% across 10 years, from 70% to 82%, by adding rate-case timing.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Wrote onboarding notes on the fund's models for new analysts.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Date of birth and nationality should be removed.
items.because: They are unrelated to the finance qualifications and can distract from them.

items.says: Experience should appear before education.
items.because: The work history should establish the candidate’s present level first.

items.says: Stonebridge Manufacturing should appear before Crescent Bank.
items.because: Newest-first ordering shows the more recent Financial Analyst role first.

items.says: Buying more fixed-rate bonds of the same duration does not hedge the existing interest-rate risk.
items.because: The additional bonds generally increase rather than offset the portfolio’s rate sensitivity.

items.says: The phrase repeats “fixed-rate.”
items.because: The wording makes the method harder to scan.

items.says: “More” does not specify the quantity or position purchased.
items.because: The wording does not tell the reader how much was purchased.

items.says: The hedge claim gives no before-and-after measure of interest-rate exposure.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the scale or effectiveness of the work from the action alone.

items.says: Reviewing declined applications does not support the claim of no rise in early defaults.
items.because: That conclusion requires comparable, properly seasoned default cohorts among newly approved applicants.

items.says: The approval-rate result should open the Crescent Bank entry.
items.because: It is the entry’s most consequential evidence.

items.says: The bullet should avoid the first-person pronoun “my.”
items.because: It adds no evidence, and résumé bullets conventionally use implied subjects.

items.says: The covenant checklist’s adoption scope is unclear.
“Writes” is the wrong tense for a role that ended in December 2022.
The forecast-error result does not say how error was calculated or compared.
The line does not show why consistent discount rates and payback rules mattered.
The reduction in manual journal entries is buried after the implementation methods.
items.because: A scanning reader may reach the technical work before seeing the strongest evidence of value.

items.says: “Mapping” uses the wrong tense for the ended role.
items.because: The present participle makes completed work sound ongoing.

items.says: The line mismatches free cash flow to equity with the weighted average cost of capital.
items.because: FCFE should normally be discounted at the cost of equity, while WACC applies to unlevered free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The valuation line gives no resulting valuation, recommendation, or decision.
items.because: The method shows analytical activity but not its usefulness to the employer.

items.says: The training and guide line gives no rollout outcome.
items.because: The reader cannot tell whether adoption, errors, cycle time, or another measure improved.

items.says: “Its” has an unclear antecedent.
The utility valuation line does not state what the valuation changed or supported.
items.because: It shows an estimate close to market price but not why the project mattered beyond producing that estimate.

items.says: The decline from USD 50 to USD 40 is 20%, not 25%.
items.because: The USD 10 decrease divided by the original USD 50 equals 20%.

items.says: “One point” does not identify the change as a percentage-point sensitivity scenario.
items.because: A finance reader needs to know how much the discount rate rose and how the scenario was run.

items.says: The change from 70% to 82% is 12 percentage points, not 12%.
items.because: The relative increase is approximately 17.1%.

items.says: “Rate-case timing” does not explain what data was added.
items.because: The shorthand leaves a general reader unsure what timing information improved the model.

items.says: The line does not identify the benchmark used to define forecast accuracy.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the model’s forecasts were compared against.

items.says: The FP&A line hides the candidate’s contribution and gives no concrete deliverable, scale, or result.
items.because: Broad labels provide little evidence of what the candidate did or whether it improved reporting, planning, or a decision.

items.says: The performance-report line should open the Student Investment Fund entry.
items.because: It is stronger evidence than the generic FP&A line.

items.says: The line does not state the return comparison or decision the report supported.
items.because: Frequent use does not establish investment impact.

items.says: The onboarding-notes line does not show what the notes enabled, their reach, or the modeling knowledge documented.
